chapter: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
title: Early New Orleans trombonists: Brunis, Gallaty, Ellibush, Perkins
summary: He assesses the trombone players he knew, who played Dixieland and who read.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Uh, you, uh, when you started on trombone though, were there any good trombone players here then?

No, not that I remembered of. The only one that I remember was Henny Brunus. He played fair trombone. He played fair trombone. And Bill Gallaty, well, he played vowel. He played a fair vowel trombone, see? And that's Joe Ellibusch, well, he was a horrible trombone player, but he... Like I tell you, he was the leader of the band, so he was the boss man, he was the trombone player.
Yeah. What about Dave Perkins? Did you ever hear him?
Yeah, Dave, brother Dave, sure I heard of Dave Perkins.
What did he play like? Was he a...
Was he a straight reader or was he a cast?
Yeah, strictly straight. Strictly straight. He didn't play no Dixieland, not to my knowledge.
What about these other fellas? Were they Dixieland trombone players? Who was that? The ones that you were talking about, like Henny Brunis.
Yeah, Henny Brunis, he was Dixieland man.
Bill Gallaty, did he play Dixieland?
Little bit, not too much. Bill was more on the legit side.
Did he read all of his stuff? No, not that I know of.
I don't think Bill ever read in his life. I'm not sure, but I don't think he did.
But he played that legit style.
